business.says: What the business says about itself (copied text): {{open}}{{value}}{{close}}
business.checks: Our own checks (internal notes, never quote them): {{value}}
business.aiNote: Our AI note (internal, never quote it): {{value}}
business.userNote: From the sender (true, and allowed to use): {{value}}
business.notWeb: Important: the sender does not sell websites. Never mention a website, or that one is missing or present.
business.nameArabicOnly: Name: it is written in Arabic letters, so do not copy it into the message. Refer to the business by its kind, for example "your clinic" or "your firm".

signals.gap: something the sender's service provides seems to be missing. Say it gently in the business's own terms, then ask whether they already have it covered.
signals.pain: customers seem to struggle with this. Show you understand the problem, with no blame, then ask a small question about it.
signals.neglect: it exists but looks dated or little used. Frame the benefit of a fresh start without criticising what they have.
signals.momentum: the business looks active and growing. Congratulate the growth briefly and ask whether they are planning the next step.

approaches.missing: Missing piece. Name, gently and in their own terms, one thing the business seems to lack that the sender's service provides, then ask whether they have it covered.
approaches.success: Build on success. Start from the good reputation shown in the facts, then suggest one natural next step the sender could help with.
approaches.fresh: Fresh start. Present an update of what they have as an easy opportunity, without criticising what exists.
approaches.timing: Timing. Tie the message to something recent or seasonal that appears in the facts or in the sender's note. If none is given, do not invent one and keep it plain.
approaches.tip: Quick tip. Offer one small, concrete and genuinely useful idea for their business, free, then ask a light question.
approaches.curiosity: Curiosity. Write one short, open question about how they handle this today, with no pitch.
